subject: Post-call recap: TelosAI dedicated SLO validation & GPU tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@telos.ai>, Marcus Chen <mchen@telos.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: TelosAI dedicated SLO validation & GPU tradeoffs

Hey Lena / Marcus —

Thanks again for taking the deep-dive with us today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Target SLOs you confirmed on the call
   - p95 latency: <= 180ms for short-chat (<=256 tokens)
   - p99 latency: <= 350ms for streaming responses when using chunked token streaming
   - Sustained throughput: 450 requests/minute for the priority route (approx 7.5 rps)
   - Concurrency target: burst to 120 concurrent sessions, steady-state ~40 concurrent streaming sessions

2) Workload notes you shared
   - Mix: 70% short chat, 20% long-form generation (512-1024 tokens), 10% embeddings/rerank
   - Streaming is used for the chat UI; low per-chunk latency matters more than raw batch throughput

3) Immediate asks from our side
   - Telos to send representative trace-level sample or small load file (see attached telos_workload_sample.json) for validation runs
   - Confirm whether p99 requirement applies to both hosted and private (you indicated private only for some EU customers — we noted US initially)

4) Redwood next steps
   - Karthik and team to propose dedicated sizing options across A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and L40S for cost/throughput tradeoffs
   - Run a targeted perf validation (3-day window) using your sample workload once we get it, include streaming emulation
   - Share a draft reserved throughput configuration and pricing worksheet (we’ll attach redwood_dedicated_pricing.xlsx)

If that looks right I’ll coordinate scheduling with Karthik for a perf design doc and a dry-run date.

Thanks —
Rafael
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127

Attachments: telos_workload_sample.json (sample traces)
From: Lena Park <lena@telos.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Chen <mchen@telos.ai>, procurement@telos.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: TelosAI dedicated SLO validation & GPU tradeoffs

Thanks Rafael — this recap looks accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- p99: yes, we want p99 <= 350ms for all customer-facing traffic in the US region. For EU customers it can be relaxed to p99 <= 500ms initially.
- Concurrency: the 120 session burst is primarily during our nightly data-scan windows when many agents reconnect; steady-state is more like 35-45.
- Streaming behavior: chunk size varies but typical token chunks are ~20-30 tokens emitted every 150-200ms. We need consistent sub-200ms chunk latency for a smooth UX.

I’ve attached an anonymized sample (see telos_workload_sample.json). It includes timestamped request/response lengths, concurrency curves, and a short list of representative prompts.

We’re okay to run a 3-day validation starting as early as 26 May. Can Redwood send preferred time slots? Also adding procurement on cc for any contract/tiers/po questions.

— Lena
Head of Product | TelosAI
lena@telos.ai
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@telos.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: TelosAI dedicated SLO validation & GPU tradeoffs

Perfect — thanks for the sample Lena. Karthik, Marissa: assigning to you both to draft the validation plan and a sizing memo. 

Initial thinking (high level):
- H100-80GB baseline: best raw latency for decoder models and superior streaming tail behavior; expect ~20-30% better p99 on short-chat vs A100 when token-by-token latency matters. Good for UX-critical routes but higher cost.
- A100-80GB baseline: strong all-around performer for throughput and long-form generation; better token throughput per dollar for batchy long-form workloads.
- L40S (or equivalent Ampere T4-class) as a cost-optimized option for non-critical routes and rerank/embeddings.

Sizing ask for perf run:
- Please propose reserved capacity options in terms of vGPU slots and a target reserved rps (e.g., reserved 12 rps, burst 20 rps) and how that maps to our Dedicated pools. Include expected p95/p99 numbers from previous benchmark runs.

Grace: can you prep a quick pricing delta table (attach to the worksheet) that shows monthly committed cost for each GPU type at the three reserved throughput points (low/medium/high)?

I’ll propose run windows 26–28 May and 2–4 June to Telos; lean on the first if you can get infra ready.

Rafael
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: TelosAI dedicated SLO validation & GPU tradeoffs

All — drafting the perf validation plan and initial bench matrix. High-level notes here before I add numbers to the shared sheet: 

Perf matrix (short):
- Workload profiles: chat-short (<=256 tokens), chat-long (512-1024 tokens, streaming enabled), batch-rerank (300–600 items)
- Targets to simulate: steady 7.5 rps, burst to 20 rps for 10-minute windows, concurrency profile matching provided curve (attached sample)

GPU comparison approach:
- H100-80GB: run single-instance microbenchmarks for token latency (p50/p95/p99) at seq=128 and seq=512. Run streaming emulation (20-token chunks every 160ms). Expect the best tail behavior due to improved transformer kernels and NVLink improvements.
- A100-80GB: run same microbenchmarks; expect slightly higher p99 for short-chat but better sustained throughput for long sequences.
- Cost-optimized nodes (L40S): confirm capability for streaming but limit to non-priority routes; quantify token/sec and memory headroom.

Validation plan:
- Day 0: dry run with synthetic load derived from telos_workload_sample.json to validate harness and telemetry.
- Day 1–2: steady-state + burst tests against each GPU type, capture token-level latency, KV-cache hit ratios, and streaming chunk latency.
- Day 3: soak test for 4 hours at expected steady concurrency and one engineered storm (120 concurrent sessions) to validate graceful degradation and fallback rules.

Deliverables: bench report (pdf), raw traces (gz), recommended Dedicated pool config (vGPU counts), and expected monthly committed cost estimates per pool.

I’ll populate the shared Drive doc and ping when numbers land.

— Karthik
Senior Infra PM | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: TelosAI dedicated SLO validation & GPU tradeoffs

Thanks — good plan. Confirming we can start the perf run on 26 May (26–28 works). A couple practical items from procurement: 

- Please send a 3-day evaluation order form or trial PO. We need the monthly committed pricing buckets for A100 vs H100 vs L40S to approve the trial cluster in our budget system.
- For the perf harness, please ensure token-level logs are anonymized (no PII) — our security team will validate.
- If the H100 option demonstrates >20% p99 improvement for chat-short at reasonable incremental cost, we have internal buy signals to push to the executive team.

Attaching a short security checklist we’ll need completed prior to the run and looping procurement.

Marcus
Director of Engineering | TelosAI
